pinyin: xīn yǒu yú ér lì bù zú
gloss: The heart is willing, but the strength is insufficient.
teaser: Ever felt motivated but unable to act? This idiom captures that feeling perfectly.
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever felt motivated but unable to act? This idiom captures that feeling perfectly.[break 1s] The phrase is: 心有余而力不足, xīn yǒu yú ér lì bù zú.[break 0.5s] 心 (xīn) - heart, mind [break 0.5s] 有 (yǒu) - to have [break 0.5s] 余 (yú) - surplus, excess [break 0.5s] 而 (ér) - but [break 0.5s] 力 (lì) - strength, power [break 0.5s] 不足 (bù zú) - insufficient, lacking [break 1s] So, the full idiom means 心有余而力不足, which literally translates to 'the heart is willing, but the strength is insufficient,' reflecting a desire to do something that one lacks the ability to accomplish.[break 1s] Here’s the story behind it:[break 1.5s] The idiom originates from a tale in ancient China where a man wanted to climb a mountain, driven by his enthusiasm and determination. However, despite his strong desire to reach the summit, his physical strength was not enough to carry him there. This contrast between aspiration and ability led to the saying we use today.[break 1.5s] Here are three examples: 他心有余而力不足，虽然想帮助朋友，但却无能为力。[break 1s] He has the will to help his friend, but he is powerless to do so. [break 1s] 这位老年人心有余而力不足，想参加马拉松，但身体不允许。[break 1s] This elderly person wants to participate in the marathon, but his body won’t allow it. [break 1s] 她心有余而力不足，想学新技能，但工作太忙。[break 1s] She wants to learn new skills, but she's too busy with work. [break 1s] So, remember: 心有余而力不足 means 'the heart is willing, but the strength is insufficient.' Thanks for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom.[break 1s]
